column1: # flow_ref 1 source=tests/spec/flow_semantics/when_values.onsa tests=10 evaluated=10 unavailable=0 skipped=0 waiting=0
@ a condition that always holds changes nothing: a literal, a block value, an init value
@ a condition that never holds leaves the output at T.default() for the whole run
@ a block condition is read once for each call of process, so the calls cut where the part stops and runs again
@ the part runs on the frames where the condition holds, and its grid of sample / 2 counts the runs, not the frames
process 0 frames=8 in c=[true true false true false false true true]
@ the delays of the part count its runs: a stopped frame is no sample of the part
process 0 frames=8 in c=[true true false true false true true true]
@ sample_tick() in the part is the time of the caller, which goes on while the part is stopped; the grid of its own stage counts the runs
process 0 frames=8 in c=[true true false true false false true true]
process 1 frames=8 in c=[true true false true false false true true]
@ S-1218: the part under down 4 inside a when~ counts the runs of the part, and reads the time of the caller divided by 4
process 0 frames=16 in c=[false true true false true true true true false true true false true true true true]
@ x.when~(a).when~(b) runs on the frames where both hold
process 0 frames=8 in a=[true true true false true true false true]
@ the calls of process cut the frames anywhere, a stopped stretch and 0 frames too: the same values (§13.4)
process 0 frames=3 in c=[false true true]
@ reset puts the part and its last output back: the next frame is as after init, in the middle of a grid and while the part is stopped
process 0 frames=3 in c=[true true true]
process 0 frames=4 in c=[true true true true]
process 0 frames=3 in c=[true true false]
process 0 frames=4 in c=[false false true true]
